analysis.investment_thesis: Shipwaves Online is a micro-cap (INR 49 Cr) digital freight forwarder with flashy ratios (ROE 56%, P/E 5.4) but negligible scale, no track record, and sits outside my circle of competence in consumer/retail. At INR 4.37 it looks statistically cheap, but tiny logistics tech outfits with unproven moats are not the boring compounders I buy.
key_strengths: Healthy headline returns — ROE 56.1%, ROCE 35.4% suggest asset-light model
Low optical P/E of 5.42 and reasonable promoter holding at 67.36%
Debt-light services business model, fits capital-efficiency preference
key_risks: Market cap of only INR 49 Cr — illiquid, limited operating history since 2015
Freight forwarding is hyper-competitive, low-margin, with no durable moat
High ROE on tiny equity base is easily distorted; earnings likely volatile
red_flags: Micro-cap SME-type scrip with thin disclosure and limited multi-year financials
Industry prone to cyclical shipping rates and disruption from larger platforms
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The numbers on paper look attractive — a 5.4x P/E with 56% ROE and 35% ROCE is the kind of ratio screen that catches attention. But I have spent decades learning that in micro-caps of INR 49 Cr, these percentages are arithmetic quirks on small equity bases, not evidence of a durable franchise. Digital freight forwarding is a brutally competitive, commoditised space where global players and well-funded startups compete on thin margins; a 2015-incorporated player has not yet seen a full shipping cycle to prove earnings quality.

My circle is consumer retail, FMCG and conservative financials — steady, predictable cash compounders where I can forecast demand ten years out. Shipwaves fails the "boring and predictable" test: logistics rates swing wildly, client concentration is likely high, and there is no brand moat. Even if promoter holding at 67.36% is adequate, I need multi-year audited consistency, dividend history, and scale before committing capital. I pass.
